subject: RFI: Tenant wrapping keys, HSM provisioning & escrow process (Helios Health)
messages:
From: Maya Green <security@helioshealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Thomas <cthomas@helioshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: RFI: Tenant wrapping keys, HSM provisioning & escrow process

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We're kicking off a short RFI to understand Redwood's approach for tenant key separation and HSM-based provisioning. Our primary asks are:

- Do you support per-tenant wrapping keys (tenant-derived DEKs) where customer-managed keys are used only to wrap a short-lived platform key?
- If a customer wants BYOK with import into a managed HSM, what import formats and attestation steps do you support?
- How do you handle key escrow/backups and recovery without ever storing customer plaintext keys?
- What TLS profiles do you mandate between customer clients and the Redwood control plane and between control plane and HSMs?

I've attached our Appendix (Helios_RFI_Sec_Appendix.xlsx) with a checklist. Can you provide a short written response and any evidentiary artifacts you can share (architecture diagram, HSM model, attestation process)?

We need this before our security review on Jan 22. If we need to set a call to go into technical detail, please propose 30–45 min slots.

Appreciate it,
Maya
Maya Green
Head of Information Security
Helios Health


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Green <security@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Cara Thomas <cthomas@helioshealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFI: Tenant wrapping keys, HSM provisioning & escrow process

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear checklist and timeline. Below is a concise response; I've attached our HSM whitepaper and a tenant wrapping diagram for visibility. I'll also produce an evidence packet (logs, config snippets, attestation examples) by Jan 20.

1) Per-tenant wrapping model
- Redwood supports a double-envelope approach: each tenant has a long-lived Customer Master Key (CMK) that is either Redwood-managed or customer-imported into a managed HSM. We never encrypt tenant data directly with the CMK. Instead, the runtime generates ephemeral Platform DEKs (data encryption keys) per deployment or shard; those DEKs are wrapped with the tenant CMK.
- We also support tenant-specific ephemeral wrapping keys (TSK) derived using an HMAC-KDF from the CMK to provide an additional separation layer for multitenant runtime shards.

2) BYOK import and attestation
- Supported import formats: PKCS#12 (.p12) and raw-binary key blobs for compatible HSMs. For customer-managed HSMs we use an agreed onboarding flow that includes key import via secure transport (mutual TLS + signed CSR).
- Attestation: for managed HSMs we provide FIPS 140-2 / 140-3 level reports and HSM module serial numbers. Where available we provide a measured boot / quote (e.g., Intel SGX or HSM attestation token) and signed Key Import logs exported from the HSM (timestamped, signed).

3) Key escrow and backups
- Redwood does not store plaintext customer keys. Escrow is implemented as an encrypted key-envelope stored in an encrypted vault; the envelope is only decryptable with a quorum-based rewrap operation that requires either (a) customer approval via our control plane + eKYC flow or (b) an authorized Redwood SRE action with multi-person approval.
- For customers requiring no escrow we offer an explicit ‘‘zero-escrow’’ contract option: Redwood will refuse to keep any recoverable backups of the unwrapped materials; recovery becomes the customer's responsibility (we document recommended procedures).

4) Rotation and lifecycle
- Recommended rotation cadence: tenant DEKs are rotated per deployment lifecycle (e.g., on reboot or key expiration). CMKs (customer-managed) can be rotated per customer policy; if an imported CMK is rotated in-customer, Redwood will perform an atomic rewrap of active DEKs on a rolling basis with a configurable window (default 48 hours).

5) TLS profiles and transport
- Control plane (API) to customer: TLS 1.2 (>=1.2) with preferred 1.3, ECDHE key exchange, AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305).
- Control plane to HSM: mutual TLS with client certs, mTLS cipher suites pinned; we also support IPsec tunnels for on-prem HSMs.

Attachments included: redwood-hsm-whitepaper.pdf, redwood-tenant-wrapping-diagram.png

If you want more low-level artifacts (HSM boot logs, sample import CSR, or a test import run), we can produce an evidence packet under an NDA and share via a short-lived Drive link. Proposed call windows: Jan 19 (10:00–11:00 EST) or Jan 20 (14:00–15:00 EST).

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik, that was helpful. A few clarifying questions from our engineering/security team:

- For the quorum-based rewrap, can you outline who holds keys to unlock the quorum? Is it strictly a set of Redwood SRE accounts + the customer's admin cert? We need to understand the split of control.
- Can you confirm whether any plaintext keys are ever exported from your environment in the case of platform disaster recovery?
- For HSM models, do you have a preferred vendor for managed HSMs? If customers bring their own HSMs on-prem, what minimum firmware/feature set do you require?

Also please share an example of the signed key import log and a sample HSM attestation token (redacted if needed).

If we could get answers and the evidence packet by EOD Jan 20 that would keep us on schedule.

Regards,
Maya


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Green <security@helioshealth.com>, Cara Thomas <cthomas@helioshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:16:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: RFI: Tenant wrapping keys, HSM provisioning & escrow process — internal: evidence and approvals

Folks — forwarding the thread. Maya asked for specifics on our quorum model, export behavior, and HSM vendor requirements. Suggested plan below; please review and I can send the final response and evidence packet tomorrow.

Suggested answers (draft):
- Quorum model: 2-of-3 quorum where keys to unlock the escrow envelope are split between: (1) a customer-held admin cert (their CMK's private import credential), (2) Redwood's KMS operator key (kept in a separate HSM cluster with strict RBAC), and (3) an offline escrow key stored in a cold-HSM escrow appliance. Activation requires any two parties. For customers that opt out of escrow we mark the envelope non-recoverable.
- Export behavior: Redwood never exports plaintext keys. In platform disaster recovery we rely on encrypted envelopes; rewrap requires the quorum. We can demonstrate via audit logs showing no instance of unwrapped key export.
- HSM vendor/firmware: preferred vendors: Thales (nShield), AWS CloudHSM, and SafeNet. Minimums for on-prem: FIPS 140-2 Level 2+ with secure key import API, support for PKCS#11 and ability to generate signed import logs. For air-gapped installs we require an approved maintenance window and a signed runbook.

Attachments to include in the evidence packet: sample_signed_import_log.txt (redacted), hsm_attestation_sample.jwt (redacted), config_snippet_kms_policy.json (redacted), and the architecture diagram.

We should also propose a 45-min technical deep-dive with Helios engineers to walk through a test import. I recommend Monday Jan 20, 14:00 EST. Lauren/Aditya: can you take the evidence assembly?

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Maya,

Per our plan, attached is the evidence packet (evidence-packet-helio.zip) containing:
- redacted sample_signed_import_log.txt (signed, timestamped by HSM)
- hsm_attestation_sample.jwt (measured-boot attestation token, redacted)
- config_snippet_kms_policy.json (example KMS policy used for tenant key ops)
- redwood-tenant-wrapping-diagram.png
- redwood-hsm-whitepaper.pdf

Quick answers to your clarifying questions:
- Quorum specifics: default 2-of-3 as described. The customer admin cert is always one of the three when escrow is enabled. The offline escrow appliance is physically isolated and uses a sealed key ceremony for recovery events; we record all actions in an immutable audit ledger.
- Plaintext export: no plaintext customer keys are exported or persistently accessible outside HSM memory. During a controlled recovery operation keys are decrypted inside the HSM and used only within HSM boundaries; we can provide audit logs showing the operation with HSM-signed timestamps.
- Preferred HSM vendors and firmware: Thales nShield and AWS CloudHSM are our most common; for on-prem customers we require firmware that supports signed import logging and remote attestation. Minimum requirement: PKCS#11 v2.40-compatible import API and FIPS 140-2 level 2 (Level 3 for high-sensitivity deployments).

I've shared a secure Drive folder with time-limited access: https://drive.redwood.com/s/secure/helio-rfi-evidence (expires in 7 days).

Let's confirm the technical deep-dive for Jan 20 at 14:00 EST (calendar invite sent separately). If you'd like, we can include a short demo of a test import into a pre-production HSM.

Best regards,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
